On 6 December 1917 the Finnish parliament adopted a declaration of independence from Russia. 6 December is Finland's Independence Day.

After the Russian Revolution of February 1917 Finland's autonomy was in question. When the Bolsheviks took power in November, the Finnish Senate under Pehr Evind Svinhufvud put forward the declaration. Lenin's government recognised it on the last day of 1917.

Independence did not bring peace. Within weeks the country fell into the Finnish Civil War between Reds and Whites. Finland then became a republic in 1919. It followed more than a century as the Grand Duchy, and the first parliament in Europe to include women, elected in 1907. See Finland.
sum: On 6 December 1917 the Finnish parliament adopted a declaration of independence from Russia. 6 December is Finland's Independence Day.
